claims.text: Lightweight HEAs can simultaneously combine low density, high mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance when they are chemically homogeneous, single-phase solid solutions with moderate lattice distortion.
Moderate lattice distortion enhances solid-solution strengthening.
Moderate lattice distortion promotes high interstitial-vacancy recombination.
High interstitial-vacancy recombination facilitates formation of coherent protective oxide and passive films.
Elemental segregation or brittle intermetallic formation causes the proposed strengthening, corrosion, and oxidation benefits to be lost.
A combination of low-density elements such as Al and Ti with mid- to high-density transition metals can provide a lightweight HEA starting composition.
Rapid solidification or optimized powder metallurgy can produce a single-phase, homogeneous, fine-grained microstructure with minimal segregation.
Controlled annealing followed by rapid quenching promotes chemical homogenization and a moderate degree of lattice distortion.
Slower cooling encourages elemental segregation and intermetallic precipitation.
Chemical short-range order and lattice distortion mediate the resulting mechanical and environmental properties.
Uniform grain size and absence of brittle secondary phases correlate with formation of a coherent, adherent oxide or passive layer.
A homogeneous single-phase HEA provides robust solid-solution strengthening.
Interstitial-vacancy recombination retards defect clustering.
Chemical homogeneity prevents inhomogeneous oxidation and thereby facilitates continuous, adherent oxide and passive films.
Segregation creates locally altered compositions that can precipitate brittle intermetallics or disrupt protective-scale formation.
The homogenized sample will have approximately 10–20% higher yield and ultimate tensile strength than the segregated sample.
The homogenized sample will exhibit lower oxidation mass gain and a more protective, uniform oxide scale than the segregated sample.
The homogenized sample will have a lower corrosion rate than the segregated sample.
Too little lattice distortion limits strengthening, whereas excessive distortion induces brittle behavior and hinders protective-scale formation.
Sustained temperatures far above 800 °C can promote phase separation and negate the benefits of initial homogeneity.
